tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.
notes: Do not infer absence from empty scoped searches; begin with null filters because missing timestamp/service fields can hide useful records.
Prefer canonical ingress/request/error logs over derived connection or refresh views.
Need concrete scope: identify affected tenant(s), workflow(s), trigger instance(s), and whether all Slack channels/events stopped or only one configuration path.
If no ingress is observed, prioritize Slack app event-subscription configuration and routing hypotheses over trigger-worker backlog theories.
If ingress is observed but verification fails, compare signing secret/raw body handling versus app settings change.
If ingress is healthy and acknowledgements succeed but workflows stay idle, inspect trigger creation, event-kind selection, channel membership, and connected-account identity changes.
Compare queue depth/processing latency around the window to rule in or out trigger-worker saturation as a broader internal regression.
Historical similar cases and deployment timing can prioritize checks, but are not proof without matching current records.

tasks.question: Starting with null filters, what canonical records show the affected Slack trigger executions and webhook ingress between 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z and 2026-11-12T10:15:00Z: were Slack event deliveries received at all, were they rejected before trigger creation, or did they stop before reaching the platform? Also compare failure rate, latency, queue/backlog, and tenant impact for the affected tenant versus at least one unaffected Slack-trigger tenant in the same window.
notes: Canonical trigger-worker log for the affected tenant shows the observed failed execution never reached platform ingress: cedar req-45 at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z recorded `provider_event_created=true`, `app_event_webhook_url=https://other.example.invalid/events`, expected ingress `https://ingress.example.invalid/slack`, and `composio_ingress_received=false` (ev_e0da4a4f4911 / slack-ingress-045:logs:0; also ev_0f6e4180abd9 / slack-ingress-045:logs:0). On the observed request, this points to Slack events stopping before reaching the platform rather than being received then rejected before trigger creation.

Tenant comparison in the same window shows cedar impact without platform-request failures: cedar metrics at 10:05 had 704 requests, 0 failures, 410 business operations blocked, queue_depth 126, p95 latency 1680 ms, versus maple with 582 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms (ev_805d726b2db1 / slack-ingress-045:metrics:0 and slack-ingress-045:metrics:1). This is consistent with tenant-scoped impact and backlog on cedar, not a broad Slack/provider outage.

Comparison records for an unaffected tenant show Slack/provider availability was not generally broken in the window: maple had a 200-status trigger-worker log with `same_provider_available=true` and `unrelated_read_succeeds=true` at 10:05 (ev_e0da4a4f4911 / slack-ingress-045:logs:1; also ev_2cc69a606e4e / slack-ingress-045:logs:1). Dependencies also report provider API reachable for trigger-worker (ev_dbcf1bd552ed / slack-ingress-045:dependencies:0).

Important gaps/counter-evidence limits: the supplied canonical evidence does not include raw ingress/webhook access logs for 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z, so absence of ingress can only be stated for the observed failed execution, not every possible Slack event in the window; there was also no trigger-worker deployment in scope to explain a platform regression (ev_0bd634ea5b09 returned no records), while the only listed deployment was unrelated support-dashboard at 10:05 (ev_3ea0d03cd005 / slack-ingress-045:deployments:0).

tasks.question: What exact app settings change occurred immediately before 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z, and did it alter Slack event subscriptions, request URL/signing secret, app scopes, workspace approval/policy state, channel membership, or connected-account identity? Check change timing against any deployment or config rollout, but treat timing only as a hypothesis until matched to canonical request records.
notes: Observed canonical request record for affected tenant cedar shows Slack event creation succeeded but the app’s event subscription webhook URL was set to `https://other.example.invalid/events` instead of expected `https://ingress.example.invalid/slack`, and no Composio ingress was received (ev_e0da4a4f4911/slack-ingress-045:logs:0; also ev_0f6e4180abd9/slack-ingress-045:logs:0). Controlled sandbox comparison matches this: original misconfigured webhook URL fails, corrected webhook URL delivers ingress (ev_c2145cce1576/slack-ingress-045:reproduce:0, slack-ingress-045:reproduce:1).

There is no canonical change/audit record here establishing the exact app-settings edit immediately before 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z or who made it. From supplied evidence, the only concrete changed setting we can identify is the Slack event subscription request URL/webhook URL mismatch; we do not have canonical records showing any contemporaneous change to signing secret, app scopes, workspace approval/policy, channel membership, or connected-account identity.

Deployment timing does not currently support an internal rollout explanation: no trigger-worker deployments were recorded from 09:00Z to 10:15Z (ev_0bd634ea5b09, no records), and the only listed deployment was an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z (ev_3ea0d03cd005/slack-ingress-045:deployments:0). Treat any timing correlation as only a hypothesis.

Impact appears tenant-specific rather than provider-wide: cedar had 704 requests, 0 transport failures, 410 business operations blocked, queue depth 126, p95 1680 ms, while comparison tenant maple had 582 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked ops, queue depth 0, p95 160 ms (ev_805d726b2db1/slack-ingress-045:metrics:0, slack-ingress-045:metrics:1). Maple also had unrelated Slack/provider reads succeed (ev_e0da4a4f4911/slack-ingress-045:logs:1; ev_2cc69a606e4e/slack-ingress-045:logs:1), which is counter-evidence to a general Slack/provider outage.

tasks.question: Among competing explanations—provider event ingress misrouting, webhook secret mismatch/body transformation, subscription event missing, workspace policy/app setting regression, scope or channel-membership change, wrong/old connection, or internal trigger-worker regression—which best matches the first failing request and what discriminating control exists (for example, unaffected tenants on the same worker, successful non-Slack webhooks, or evidence that the request never reached the provider/platform)?
notes: Best match for the first failing request: provider_event_ingress_misrouting.
Best discriminating control: corrected-versus-original webhook URL comparison showing ingress restored only when the Slack event subscription URL matched expected ingress.
No trigger-worker deployment in scope was evidenced; the only listed deployment was unrelated, so deployment timing is not a persuasive primary cause here.

hypothesis.description: The first observed failing Slack trigger request for tenant cedar was caused by Slack app event-subscription misrouting: the app's configured webhook URL pointed to a different endpoint than the expected platform ingress, so the event was created upstream but never reached Composio ingress.
assumptions: Conclusion is scoped to the observed first failing request and the cedar tenant evidence, not every possible Slack event in the full window.
The sandbox controlled comparison verifies the webhook URL variable, not every possible Slack app setting.

findings.statement: For cedar request req-45, trigger-worker recorded provider_event_created=true, app_event_webhook_url=https://other.example.invalid/events, expected_ingress_url=https://ingress.example.invalid/slack, and composio_ingress_received=false. This directly matches event ingress misrouting and shows the failed execution never reached platform ingress.

A controlled sandbox comparison changed only Slack configuration: with the original webhook URL pointing to other.example.invalid, ingress was not received; with the corrected webhook URL pointing to the expected ingress, the same kind of provider event reached Composio ingress. This is the clearest discriminating control.

Impact was tenant-specific rather than provider-wide: cedar had 704 requests, 0 transport failures, 410 business operations blocked, queue depth 126, p95 latency 1680 ms, while maple had 582 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked operations, queue depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms.

A comparison tenant on the same worker had successful unrelated Slack/provider activity, and dependencies reported provider API reachable. This is counter-evidence to a broad Slack/provider outage or platform-wide ingress failure.

No trigger-worker deployment was recorded in scope, while the only listed deployment was an unrelated support-dashboard release. This weakens an internal regression explanation based on rollout timing.

actions: Restore the Slack app event-subscription request URL/webhook URL to the expected ingress endpoint and verify with a newly generated channel message.
Collect canonical Slack app settings or audit evidence for the 09:50-10:15 window to confirm when the request URL changed and whether any other Slack setting changed at the same time.
Align ingress and application telemetry for the incident window before generalizing this cause to all missed events.
missing_checks: Canonical Slack app settings/audit evidence for the cedar app around 09:50-10:15 to confirm the exact production configuration change and rule out additional simultaneous Slack app edits.
Canonical ingress/webhook access logs for the full window to verify whether all missed cedar events shared the same never-reached-ingress pattern.

hypothesis.description: A signing-secret mismatch is a weaker alternative if Slack did reach the platform and was rejected during verification after the app settings change.
assumptions: This would require ingress attempts not present in the supplied canonical records.

findings.statement: The observed failed cedar request shows composio_ingress_received=false with a mismatched app_event_webhook_url, so the current evidence points to delivery to the wrong destination before any in-platform signature check could occur.
Correcting the webhook URL alone restored ingress in the controlled comparison, which argues against secret mismatch as the primary explanation for the first observed failure.

actions: Only investigate signing-secret alignment if canonical ingress logs later show requests reaching the platform but failing verification.
If such ingress evidence appears, compare the active Slack signing secret and platform verifier configuration for the affected app.
missing_checks: Canonical ingress verification logs showing whether any Slack requests reached the platform and failed signature validation during the incident window.

hypothesis.description: A workspace policy or Slack app settings regression is a broader category that could explain why the webhook URL became wrong, but the immediate first-failure mechanism is still misrouting rather than a policy block proven in evidence.
assumptions: The incident title mentions an app settings change, but there is no canonical audit trail here proving a workspace policy action or admin approval change.
This is relevant as an upstream reason for misconfiguration, not as the direct observed failure mechanism.

findings.statement: The only concrete changed state visible in supplied records is the wrong Slack event-subscription webhook URL on the failing cedar request.
Another tenant on the same worker had successful provider activity, which does not fit a broad internal or provider outage and leaves room for tenant-specific Slack app configuration causes.

actions: Request workspace-admin or Slack app audit evidence only to determine who or what changed the app settings that produced the wrong webhook URL.
Review tenant-specific Slack app configuration history before considering broader workspace policy explanations.
missing_checks: Slack workspace/app audit records establishing whether a policy action or admin edit changed the event subscription settings at incident start.
